entries.label: vendor-claim
entries.claim: Homepage FAQ: a free account gets four humanizations of up to 250 words, one-time, no card; the AI detector is free without an account. Rechecked live 2026-09-12.
entries.quote: Yes. A free account gets 4 humanizations at up to 250 words each, with no credit card. The four runs are a one-off welcome allowance rather than a daily reset, since each run uses real compute. The AI detector needs no account at all, and when you want more, paid plans start at $12/mo billed yearly or $18/mo monthly.

recaptures.claim: Free account: four rewrites of up to 250 words, no card; Basic $12/mo annual ($144/yr), $18 monthly; Pro $18/$27; Ultra $36/$48. Homepage: detector 250 words, four times a day, no account. Unchanged.
Unchanged: free account four humanizations of up to 250 words, no card; detector 250 words, four times a day, no account.

entries.quote: HumanizeMyAI is built and operated by Fırat Mıhcı, an ESL writing researcher. ... The product is a research project that became a product, not a product retrofitted with a research narrative.

entries.label: vendor-claim

entries.quote: Humanize / detect inputs: the text you paste into the tool is sent to our LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI) for processing and a detector vendor (GPTZero) for scoring. We do not retain your inputs after the request completes. We do not train our models on your inputs.

entries.quote: Subscriptions are recurring. ... You can cancel at any time from your account page, and cancellation stops all future charges while leaving your access intact until the end of the period you already paid for.

entries.label: vendor-claim
entries.claim: Generally non-refundable after access, with defined exceptions.
entries.quote: Paid subscription charges are generally non-refundable after digital access is provided. We will issue or consider a refund when required by applicable law, when a duplicate or incorrect charge occurred, or when a documented material service failure prevented access to the paid service.

entries.label: research-finding
entries.claim: Recursive paraphrasing reduces detector performance with some quality cost.
entries.quote: Our findings indicate that while our recursive paraphrasing method can significantly reduce detection rates, it only slightly degrades text quality in many cases, highlighting potential vulnerabilities in current detection systems in the presence of an attacker.

entries.label: research-finding
entries.claim: Evaluated detectors were neither accurate nor reliable; obfuscation worsened performance.

entries.label: research-finding
entries.claim: RAID benchmark covers more than six million generations and documents robustness failures.
entries.quote: RAID includes over 6 million generations spanning 11 models, 8 domains, 11 adversarial attacks and 4 decoding strategies. Using RAID, we evaluate the out-of-domain and adversarial robustness of 8 open- and 4 closed-source detectors and find that current detectors are easily fooled by adversarial attacks, variations in sampling strategies, repetition penalties, and unseen generative models.

entries.label: research-finding
entries.claim: AI detectors can misclassify non-native English writing.
entries.quote: GPT detectors frequently misclassify non-native English writing as AI generated, raising concerns about fairness and robustness.
